_readme: Configuration for the OpenRocket simulation check (design/openrocket_batch_sim/or_ci.py and
.github/workflows/openrocket-sim.yml). Every path is relative to this file.
A .ork stores only a REFERENCE to its motor; headless OpenRocket knows just the commercial motors
bundled in its jar, so team-made .rse/.eng motors must be pointed to here, per simulation name.
Resolution order per simulation and per motor mount: simulations[<name>].motors[<mount>] (or .motor when
the simulation has one mount) -> default_motors[<mount>] / default_motor -> the file's own motor
-> a .rse/.eng in the .ork's folder or its subfolders (e.g. Thrust Curves/) whose designation matches the one
A hybrid modelled as two motors (ox tank + combustion chamber) is two mounts: see SOL_4_30 below.
limits: {metric: {min, max}} checked on the current version; global here, overridable per file / simulation.
Metrics: apogee, max_velocity, max_mach, max_acceleration, velocity_off_rod, stability_off_rod_cal,
min_stability_cal, time_to_apogee, velocity_at_deployment, descent_rate, flight_time, landing_distance.
Set fail_on_limits to true once the team wants violations to turn the check red.
deterministic_wind true zeroes wind turbulence (average wind is kept) so an unchanged design reproduces
exactly; OpenRocket 24.12's turbulence is not controlled by the seed and moves stability off the rod by ~0.5 cal.

SOL_INVICTUS/OpenRocket/SOL_4_30.ork._note: Two-mount hybrid model; these would also auto-resolve by designation (OX / CC).
